title: Ring scene A key: delete the ring each sliver run drops and turn its other stretches into bisectors on its exact route

description:
In the ring scene, A removes the lens slivers two closed rings pinch where they run along each other and touch. SliverCollapse finds each lens, joins a pair's neighbouring lenses into runs (never across a gap whose inner side is a real region), and picks each run's keeper: the crease ring against a geodesic one, else the ring with more authored anchors along the run. A ring keeping one run may be dropped along another; keeper cycles and overlapping runs are refused.

The other ring, B, is deleted. Each stretch of B outside every run becomes one spline_cut bisector that follows B's old route exactly: rings and bisectors are the same spline, and each segment depends only on its two anchors and the tangents from their neighbours. The bisector carries B's spline anchors (authored and supporting) over the stretch in B's order, plus one anchor past each end inside the run, and a new `stretch` argument: B's anchor before the first and after the last, which the open spline's end tangents take as neighbours (so every segment is traced exactly as B traced it), and the two vertices where the stretch met its keepers. The node snaps the open trace to an ordered vertex walk and keeps the part between the touches of its end walls nearest those meeting points (the start before the first inner anchor, the end after the last), cutting spurs and side loops. The meeting points re-attach to their walls on every evaluation, so editing a keeper moves the trim; bisectors without `stretch` work as before. Existing bisectors that ended on B move to the nearest new wall. A checks every new bisector's edges against B's old edges over the stretch and reports any difference.

A is one undo step from any tool. ctrl+S deletes B's statement and appends the bisectors; a reload reproduces the same regions. Single-ring and three-ring slivers, and slivers walled by a bisector, are left alone.
definition-of-done:
1. On fresh copies of IMG_4109, IMG_4110 and IMG_4111, A then ctrl+S then a reload leaves zero two-ring slivers, measured in the app. Single-ring and three-ring slivers are left alone.
2. A deletes each dropped ring's statement and confirmed ring; each stretch of it outside the runs becomes a spline_cut bisector through the ring's own anchors with a stretch argument, marking exactly the ring's old edges over the stretch (A reports any that differ); bisectors that ended on it move to the new walls. BisectorFit and the fitting are gone.
3. No hidden cut state; after A every ring and bisector draws as its smooth curve (a ring stretch only between its meeting points) and edits like any other.
4. ctrl+Z after A, from any tool, restores the dropped rings and their slivers in one step; ctrl+Y redoes it.
5. A closed ring's snapped marks are always one simple cycle: a small loop hanging off it at one vertex is dropped, covered by a unit test of the snap.
6. Unit tests cover: a lens collapsed into a bisector, saved, reloaded with zero slivers; a double lens deletes the dropped ring; a crease keeper against a geodesic ring; a ring stretch marks the same edges as the ring; the collapse's bisector marks the dropped ring's own edges; a bisector moved from the dropped ring to the keeper; ctrl+Z after A through scene key dispatch.
testing-plan:
1. Unit test: synthetic mesh, two touching rings pinching a sliver; apply the reroute, serialise and re-parse the rings, rebuild RingRegions, assert slivers == 0.
2. In the app: open a crawfish model with known slivers in the ring scene, press A, ctrl+S, reload the model, and screenshot the region view and summary line showing 0 slivers (under tmp/).
unknowns: Which ring of the pair moves: the one walling the sliver off from its largest neighbour, or the shorter/less authored one?
Does a re-tightened ring with pinned reroute anchors stay where it was put on reload, or does it need a new anchor kind?
changes-made: A in the ring scene now calls RingTool.rerouteSlivers: SliverReroute (new, geometry/mesh/data/rings) moves the ring walling each sliver from its largest neighbour onto the sliver's far side, retraced as a GEODESIC spline through the ring's own anchors on the new loop plus the reroute's vertices (every loop vertex as fallback), kept only when the regions are the old ones with exactly that sliver merged; a ring walling nothing but a sliver is deleted. One undoable edit, rings marked unsaved, ctrl+S writes spline_ring statements.

The display-only absorb toggle is gone: RegionLayer.absorbSlivers/toggleAbsorbSlivers, RingRegions.rebuild's absorbBelow parameter and ui-state's regions.absorbSlivers removed. RingTool.orderedLoop moved to EdgeMarks.orderedLoop (geometry layer) with its callers.

Verified on a copy of IMG_4110: 110 regions / 39 slivers -> A -> 71 regions / 0 slivers -> ctrl+S -> reload -> 71 regions / 0 slivers, identical per-region face counts. Unit test SliverRerouteTest round-trips two pinching rings through spline_ring statements.

Rework after review: the vertex-baking SliverReroute is gone. A now runs RingTool.collapseSlivers over SliverCollapse (geometry/mesh/data/rings): every sliver walled by exactly two closed rings meeting at its two ends is a lens; the crease ring keeps it (modes differ) or the ring with more anchors along it; the other ring is dropped and each stretch of it between its lenses becomes a spline_cut bisector through its own authored anchors, in its own mode, ends attached to the keeper rings. A ring whose bisectors would pinch a new sliver (bounded local flood from the bisector edges, no region rebuild) is not dropped. Save deletes the dropped ring's statement and appends the bisectors.

IMG_4110 copy: A in 370 ms (was 5124 ms); 18 of 39 slivers collapsed, 6 rings dropped into 7 bisectors; after ctrl+S and reload 92 regions, 21 slivers, identical per-region face counts. Left: 13 slivers of the ring_49 cluster, 5 on ring_11 (not one simple loop), 3 walled by one ring.

Consecutive lenses of one ring pair that zigzag (every vertex between them on the other ring) merge into one run P..Q; the kept ring owns it, the dropped ring's bisectors end at P and Q. Single-ring slivers are reported as left on purpose, never dropped. ConformingLoopSnap drops side loops hanging off a closed ring at one vertex (ring_11's triangle at vertex 79023, the only one among 249 rings on IMG_4110, IMG_4111, crawfish_rings, fertility_rings).

IMG_4110 copy: on load 109 regions, 38 slivers (36 two-ring, 2 single-ring); A in 371 ms collapses 15, dropping 8 rings into 8 bisectors; after ctrl+S and reload 95 regions, 23 slivers (21 two-ring, 2 single-ring), same partition. The 21 left: bisectors leaving a run end nearly tangent to the kept ring pinch new slivers (ring_49 vs ring_35/43/54, ring_11 vs ring_10/15, ring_12/ring_44 run), so the guard refuses those drops.

Correction to the line above: ring_11's lenses all collapse now (ring_10 and ring_15 dropped into bisectors). The 21 two-ring slivers left are ring_12/ring_44 (8), ring_49/ring_54 (8), ring_35/ring_49 (4) and ring_43/ring_49 (1).

Each bisector gets an end anchor past each meeting point: the first vertex of the dropped ring's own path more than 4 mean edges from the kept ring (its own anchors short of that are dropped). A run refused whole is split into its lenses for a second pass. IMG_4110 copy: A in 568 ms collapses 34 of 36 two-ring slivers (ring_49 now dropped; 9 rings into 11 bisectors; 1 run needed the fallback); after reload 76 regions, 2 two-ring slivers left (ring_12/ring_48), 2 single-ring regions. The ring_12/ring_48 lenses stay because ring_12 keeps ring_44's run, and dropping ring_48 pinches a new 2-face region 17.6 mean edges from its end on ring_12.

Keepers are now chosen per cluster of rings joined by lenses: every subset of a cluster's rings (cap 12) is ranked by slivers removed, then fewest rings dropped, then the keeper rules, and the first that passes the new-sliver guard stands; above the cap the old greedy order runs. End-anchor clearance is measured against every ring the cluster keeps. A run whose rings do not meet at both its ends now also falls back to single lenses. IMG_4110 copy: A in 320 ms, clusters of 3,3,4,2,2,2,3 rings all searched exhaustively, 34 of 36 two-ring slivers collapsed; after reload 76 regions, 2 two-ring slivers (ring_12/ring_48) and 2 single-ring regions. Every choice for the ring_12/ring_44/ring_48 cluster that collapses those two fails: the best, dropping ring_12, makes its bisector from ring_48 to ring_44 pinch a new 5-face region 3.7 mean edges from its end on ring_48, inside the end-anchor clearance.

Redesign: SliverCollapse keeps a run on one ring and cuts the other along it (RingCut), no retrace; spline_ring gains cut_by and cuts; the ring tool cuts, draws the pieces, saves cut rings after their keepers, re-adopts the cut on reload and re-cuts when a keeper is edited. Removed the bisector conversion, end anchors and cluster search. After ctrl+S and reload: IMG_4110 0 two-ring slivers (2 single-ring), IMG_4109 48 (from 198), IMG_4111 65 (from 126), each named in tmp/craw89/models/survivors.json: keeper conflicts (a ring keeping one run is never cut for another) and two guard refusals (ring_81 on IMG_4109, ring_21 on IMG_4111). A: 341, 462, 267 ms. ctrl+Z restores every sliver.

A ring may now keep one run and be cut along another when the two stay apart on its loop; every cut is taken from the rings as traced and applied together; keeper cycles are refused (other keeper tried first); saving orders chains keeper-first. The guard now accepts dropping an edge that borders any sliver (its two refusals were runs crossing three-ring slivers). A run no longer joins lenses across a gap whose inner side is a real region (IMG_4109 ring_03/ring_32 across a 105-face region). Editing a cut ring re-cuts it from its new trace; a run no longer found is left whole there and the row says so; undo restores. SliverCollapse reads each sliver's walling rings from RingRegions.boundingRingsByRegion (identical on all 381 slivers of the three models). After reload: IMG_4109 0 two-ring slivers (from 198), IMG_4110 0 (from 36), IMG_4111 45 (from 126), all 45 between crease rings that spline_cut bisectors end on. A: 441, 189, 182 ms; guard fired 0 times.

A now cuts rings that bisectors end on. A bisector end inside a cut stretch (every edge the cut ring had at that vertex dropped) moves to the keeper of that run (of the rings it was cut along, the nearest), its statement's ends rewritten on save, in the same undo step; an end at a run's end point P or Q stays on the cut ring, which keeps an edge there; a bisector that would wall nothing once moved leaves its cut rings whole. Moved ends never move back when a keeper or the cut ring is edited later; the row says so when an edited cut ring loses a run. Refusals now name each ring's own reason. The headless replay is dropped; all numbers come from the app. After reload: IMG_4109 0 two-ring slivers, IMG_4110 0, IMG_4111 1 (ring_06/ring_50 meet at only one end of that lens). A: 991, 189, 237 ms. 1 bisector end moved (IMG_4111). Guard fired 0 times.

Stretch ends now meet when they are the same vertex or joined by edges both rings mark (RingCut.endsMeet), for single lenses and runs; the cut point is the cut ring's own end of the shared stretch, which lies on the keeper, so RingCut's reload re-find needs no change. Run overlap is now measured on loop edges, so lenses that only touch at an end vertex no longer block each other. After A, ctrl+S and reload: IMG_4109 0 two-ring slivers (from 198), IMG_4110 0 (from 36), IMG_4111 0 (from 126). ctrl+Z restores all. IMG_4109 A over 6 fresh launches: 810, 487, 412, 1617, 418, 490 ms (median 488).

Redesign per the user: the hidden cut state is gone (spline_ring cut_by/cuts, ConfirmedRing.cutBy/cutXyz, RingCut, RingDslWriter.appendCutRing, cut adoption, re-cuts on edit, the jagged cut-ring drawing). A now deletes the ring each run drops and turns each stretch of it outside the runs into a spline_cut bisector fitted by BisectorFit (B's spline anchors on the stretch, one anchor added where the trace strays more than about an edge or pinches a new sliver, cap max(3x starting, 1 per 8 old vertices)); dropped keepers keep junctions as anchors; existing bisectors on a dropped ring move to the nearest new wall. After A, ctrl+S, reload on fresh copies: IMG_4110 36 -> 0 two-ring slivers, IMG_4109 198 -> 30 (ring_81 and ring_32 refused: their bisectors pinch 104- and 105-face regions under the sliver size), IMG_4111 127 -> 19 (ring_30 at its anchor cap, one keeper overlap, 5 others). A: 2002, 1280, 4487 ms. ctrl+Z/ctrl+Y verified in the region and ring tools. mvn test 746/0.

Rework: bisectors follow the dropped ring's exact route. SurfaceSplineTracer takes optional lead-in/lead-out vertices for an open spline's end tangents; ConformingLoopSnap.orderedWalk snaps an open trace to an ordered vertex walk; SurfaceSpline.ringStretch traces a ring stretch through the ring's anchors and trims it at its end walls nearest the meeting points; spline_cut gains a stretch argument (ring anchor before, two meeting points, ring anchor after) that the ring tool saves, adopts, re-traces when a wall is edited and carries through re-opening and undo. SliverCollapse builds each bisector from the ring's anchors and checks its edges against the ring's (routeDifferences). BisectorFit, the anchor fitting, the anchor cap, the new-sliver refusal, the junction anchors and the per-region merge bookkeeping are deleted.

Fresh copies, measured in the app (two-ring slivers on load -> after A -> after ctrl+S and reload): IMG_4109 198 -> 0 -> 0, A 531 ms, 21 rings dropped into 43 bisectors; IMG_4110 36 -> 0 -> 0, A 224 ms, 12 into 12; IMG_4111 127 -> 4 -> 4, A 311 ms, 15 into 24 (10 from crease rings), 9 existing bisector ends moved. Every new bisector marks exactly its ring's old edges. IMG_4111's 4: one sliver of ring_02 and the existing bisector ring_68 (there on load), and three former three-ring slivers of the ring_15/ring_21/ring_50 zipper now walled by ring_15 and a new bisector; a second A press clears none, since A only collapses two closed rings. Real-region face counts change only by merged sliver faces.
review-summary: The ring scene's A key deletes the ring losing each sliver run and turns its other stretches into bisectors that follow its exact old route. Regions therefore stay where they were and survive save and reload.
